classification.difficultyReason: Foundation: explain the usefulness of each supplied graph by distinguishing an actual count from a proportion of the class. Reading 7 students and approximately 24% directly applies the taught comparison and parts-of-a-whole purposes.

inlines.text: The principal wants to see how many of Mr Ding’s class get an A.
Give reasons why he would look at either of the graphs.

spec.description: Four separated columns on a square grid extending outside the axes. Decorative column shading omitted.
spec.mathematics: A=7, B=10, C=9, D=3 students. Horizontal grid increments one student; labelled ticks 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied graph, visible in questions.

spec.description: Unfilled sector graph with external labels, clockwise from the upward radius: A, 24%; B, 35%; C, 31%; D, 10%. Source decorative sector fills are omitted because labels identify every category.
spec.mathematics: Native boundaries use the printed approximate proportions: 86.4, 126, 111.6 and 36 degrees. These are reconstruction values, not additional printed givens. Retain B, 35% under reviewed-interpretations-p54.
spec.answerVisibility: All four labels are permanent supplied data, visible in questions.

answer.short: The column graph shows 7 students get an A; the sector graph shows approximately $24\%$ of the class get an A.
answer.worked: The A column gives the actual frequency: $7$ students. The A sector gives the share of the class: approximately $24\%$. Use the column graph for the number and the sector graph for the proportion.
